correctness.rationale: The theorem specifies every n>=3 and every triple a,b,c>=0 with sum n. Length-2 edges consume same-parity pairs, so parity b even is necessary. If 3|n, a single length-1 edge leaves two odd residue classes under length-3 edges, forbidding (a,b,c)=(1,0,n-1). For b>=2 even, a concatenation of explicit B/E/F blocks, D blocks, and A blocks gives all possibilities according to c modulo 3. For b=0 and a>=(c mod 3), A/C/D suffice; the only other allowed case uses the even->even+3 modulo 2n bijection, while a=1 and c mod 3=2 is exactly the forbidden residue case. All boundaries and six signatures were checked using the packaged stand-alone verify.py: 46,748 construction cases through n=80, exact definition-based profile enumeration through n=18 with 702 realizable profiles, and VERIFY_OK. Infinite correctness rests on the direct combinatorial proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2023 two-length theorem covers any profile with at most two nonzero multiplicities; the consecutive-length corollary requires equal multiplicities and does not cover arbitrary triples. The 2016 modular-unit theorem cannot apply when b>0. A Hamiltonian path with a prescribed 2n-1-edge list does not imply a perfect matching with an independently prescribed n-edge list. The novel positive assertion is for genuinely three-supported multiplicity profiles.

originality.rationale: Closest fully inspected primary article arxiv:2308.16553v1 proves parity necessity, two-support classification, and selected equal-multiplicity lists, but sets out the prime parity question as an open conjecture. The complete unrestricted three-short-distance existence criterion and explicit six-block realization of every triple profile are not implications of those statements. The 2016 full preprint requires modular-unit distances, excluding the nonzero length-2 cases. Related Skolem-set and Hamiltonian-path formulations do not directly settle the circular matching problem. Indexed published mathematical records and relevant literature produced no equivalent theorem; residual risk of unindexed or unstated stronger prior work persists.

value.rationale: The 2023 source explicitly motivates classification when necessary parity is sufficient and conjectures a prime-order characterization. The present theorem completely determines realizability for the first unrestricted three-length support {1,2,3}, for all n and arbitrary multiplicities, with a genuine n mod 3 boundary; it resolves the three-short-distance slice of the prime conjecture. Unlike an isolated small calculation, it supplies a uniform constructive procedure and an exact impossibility criterion for an infinite natural combinatorial family. The restriction to only three lengths is motivated by the published transition from two-length classifications to three-length unknown cases.
